content.value_statement: Animation work can fail when keyframes are not deterministic or easy to verify. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through seek-safe HyperFrames motion patterns and proof steps.
actual_capabilities: Guides GSAP, CSS keyframes, Anime.js, and WAAPI setup for seek-safe animation.
Helps choose mechanisms such as FLIP, path travel, stroke draw, masks, SVG morphing, and DOM 3D.
Defines deterministic runtime rules for finite durations, fill modes, registration, and final-state holds.
Recommends focused HyperFrames diagnostics, selector shots, ghost views, and snapshots at proof times.
Provides failure fixes for endpoint-only motion, identity breaks, fake 3D, wrong finals, and unreadable text.
limitations: It does not cover broad scene strategy, brand design, media sourcing, captions, or general video planning.
It assumes HyperFrames tooling and the chosen animation library are available in the project.
It gives implementation guidance, but rendered frames still need visual inspection.
It does not replace license review for GSAP plugins or third-party animation libraries.

use_cases.title: Build motion proof frames
use_cases.description: Define visible poses, final holds, and verification moments for a HyperFrames animation.

use_cases.title: Implement deterministic timelines
use_cases.description: Choose a runtime pattern and register keyframes so renders can seek to any frame.

use_cases.title: Review animation failures
use_cases.description: Diagnose identity breaks, fake depth, unreadable text, reset tails, and missing proof poses.

prompt_templates.title: Create basic keyframes
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a simple motion pass
prompt_templates.prompt: Use hyperframes-keyframes to animate [subject] from [start state] to [final state]. Keep the final pose visible and list the proof frames to inspect.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a motion mechanism
prompt_templates.prompt: Use hyperframes-keyframes to choose between FLIP, path travel, stroke draw, mask reveal, text subdivision, or DOM 3D for [motion goal]. Explain the smallest mechanism that proves the idea.

prompt_templates.title: Debug failed verification
prompt_templates.scenario: Fixing a render that does not prove the motion
prompt_templates.prompt: Use hyperframes-keyframes to review this failed animation: [describe failure]. Identify likely causes and give source-level fixes before another diagnostic pass.

prompt_templates.title: Plan advanced 3D verification
prompt_templates.prompt: Use hyperframes-keyframes to plan seek-safe 3D or canvas keyframes for [scene]. Include camera, object, material, and snapshot proof requirements.

output_examples.input: A logo outline should draw itself, fill in, and hold on the final lockup.
output_examples.output: The skill would recommend a stroke draw mechanism, a clear mid-draw proof frame, a completed fill state, and a final lockup snapshot.

output_examples.input: A product card should move from a grid cell into a detailed hero position without looking replaced.
output_examples.output: The skill would recommend shared-element or FLIP motion, one persistent subject, geometry-derived transforms, and checks for identity continuity.

output_examples.input: A WebGL scene should show an object moving past the camera with visible depth.
output_examples.output: The skill would recommend deterministic camera and object keyframes, occlusion proof, ghosted depth checks, and snapshots at first, crossing, and final poses.

best_practices: Name the animated subject and proof poses before choosing a runtime.
Keep timelines deterministic, finite, registered, and seekable.
Verify first frame, proof poses, final-minus-hold, and exact final with visual snapshots.
anti_patterns: Relying on timers, hover, scroll, random values, or autoplay for render-critical motion.
Replacing a subject with a crossfade when continuity should be visible.
Ending with cleanup, black frames, debug overlays, or a reset state.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps create deterministic keyframes for HyperFrames compositions and verifies the visible motion.

faq.question: Which animation runtimes does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers GSAP, CSS keyframes, Anime.js, WAAPI, SVG techniques, DOM 3D, and canvas or WebGL patterns.

faq.question: Does it generate a full video plan?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on keyframe implementation and verification, not broad story, brand, or media planning.

faq.question: Can it help debug motion that looks wrong?
faq.answer: Yes. It lists common failures such as endpoint-only motion, identity breaks, fake 3D, wrong finals, and unreadable text.

faq.question: Does it require command-line tools?
faq.answer: The guidance references HyperFrames diagnostics for verification. Users should run tools only in trusted projects.

faq.question: Is it useful for 3D scenes?
faq.answer: Yes. It gives guidance for DOM 3D, Three.js, WebGL camera motion, shader uniforms, and depth verification.
